title: Akal Takht vs. Punjab: A 15-Day Ultimatum Over Sacrilege Law
excerpt: Sikhism's highest seat orders Bhagwant Mann's AAP government to strip 'objectionable clauses' or face Panthic action
body:
Sikhism's supreme temporal authority and Punjab's elected government collided openly this week — and a 15-day clock is now ticking.

**What Happened:**
On May 8, Akal Takht officiating Jathedar Giani Kuldip Singh Gargaj issued a formal ultimatum to the AAP government of CM Bhagwant Mann: remove 'objectionable clauses' from the newly enacted *Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026* within 15 days, or face strict Panthic action. The Act, passed unanimously on April 13 during a special Vaisakhi session at Sri Anandpur Sahib, imposes penalties ranging from seven years to life imprisonment for sacrilege against the Guru Granth Sahib.

**Why the Akal Takht Objects:**
Gargaj's central grievance is one of process and sovereignty. He says the draft was prepared on the night of April 11 and rushed through the assembly within two days — completely bypassing both the Akal Takht and the SGPC, despite both bodies having explicitly requested consultation. The Jathedar objects to clauses that place granthis, gurdwara committees, and ordinary Sikhs who possess a saroop of the Guru Granth Sahib within a criminal liability framework, calling it direct state interference in internal Sikh religious affairs. A particularly contentious provision requires that details of every saroop be uploaded to a government-monitored website — something the clergy insists is their own sacred responsibility.

**CM Mann Refuses to Budge:**
Mann has flatly rejected any withdrawal, touring Punjab on a 'Shukrana Yatra' (thanksgiving procession) to celebrate the law's passage. The Jathedar has called the yatra an 'ahankar yatra' — a procession of pride — and warned that ignoring Panthic institutions could compel him to convene all five Sikh high priests for collective action.

**What to Watch:**
The May 23 deadline is the pressure point — watch whether Mann's government offers amendments, the Akal Takht escalates to a formal hukamnama, or the standoff reshapes the political battlefield ahead of Punjab's expected 2027 assembly elections.
